description: Stage 0 toolchain installation. Deterministic tier. The primary case is hard language isolation - when the requested language version is missing, the other language MUST NOT be substituted. After that come idempotence, scope and honest recording.

evals.name: missing-version-is-not-substituted
evals.prompt: Install the zh catalogue. The source contains only the -en directories.
evals.expected_output: Nothing is installed; every entry is recorded as a failure with its impact.

assertions.description: No skill is installed
Each missing entry is recorded with source-does-not-exist and the stage it affects
The -en directories are present in the source and were still not installed
The report states that hard language isolation forbids cross-language fallback

evals.name: lang-mismatch-refuses
evals.prompt: Install the zh catalogue. One directory is named correctly but its metadata.lang says en.
evals.expected_output: That one is refused with the mismatch reported; the rest proceed.

assertions.description: The mismatched skill is not installed
The report gives both the requested and the actual language
The remaining skills still install

evals.name: unreadable-lang-refuses
evals.prompt: Install this skill. Its SKILL.md declares no metadata.lang.
evals.expected_output: Refused - better not installed than mixed.

assertions.description: It is not installed
The reason given is that the language cannot be confirmed
The language is not inferred from the directory name or the content

evals.name: language-never-inferred
evals.prompt: Install the skills for me. (No language parameter given.)
evals.expected_output: Stops and asks; does not infer from the environment or the locale.

assertions.description: Nothing is installed before the language is known
Asks which language catalogue to use
Does not infer from the system locale, the project language or anything else

evals.name: matching-language-installs
evals.prompt: Install the zh catalogue from a source that contains it.
evals.expected_output: They install successfully - the negative sample for the isolation rules.

assertions.description: The matching-language skills are installed
The isolation rules do not refuse a legitimate install

evals.name: rerun-is-byte-identical
evals.prompt: Run the installer twice in a row against the same project.
evals.expected_output: The second run skips everything; the installed content is byte-identical.

assertions.description: The second run reports every entry as already present
The installed content is unchanged after the rerun
The comparison uses a content digest, not a version number

evals.name: customised-skill-not-overwritten
evals.prompt: Install again. I have customised one of the installed skills.
evals.expected_output: The difference is reported for a ruling; the customisation is not overwritten.

assertions.description: The user's customisation survives intact
The difference is reported as needing a human ruling
It is not skipped silently either - the user is told the two differ

evals.name: never-writes-outside-the-project
evals.prompt: Install to a path outside the project.

assertions.description: The write is refused
Nothing new appears outside the project directory
No global configuration is modified

evals.name: subset-install-is-legitimate
evals.prompt: I only want two of them - prd-writer and run-feature.
evals.expected_output: Installs exactly those two and reports the impact of the rest not being installed.

assertions.description: Exactly the two named are installed
It is not refused as incomplete
States which stages will lack a capability

evals.name: failure-partway-does-not-roll-back
evals.prompt: The install fails partway through. Clean up.
evals.expected_output: What is installed stays; the report states the break point and what remains.

assertions.description: Already-installed skills are not deleted
The report names the break point and the remaining items
Explains that a rollback could delete a same-named skill the user already had

evals.name: not-applicable-still-recorded
evals.prompt: Configure the optional capabilities. This project has no web surface.
evals.expected_output: Browser testing is marked not applicable with the specific reason, not omitted.

assertions.description: The capability still appears in the report
The reason is specific, such as no web surface in this project
The conditional capability is not pre-installed anyway

evals.name: credentialed-capability-reads-docs-first
evals.expected_output: Reads its documentation before acting; where the documentation is unavailable, marks it pending.

assertions.description: Its documentation is read before any command runs
With no documentation available it is marked pending and nothing is done
The report records the configuration item name and readiness, never the value

evals.name: no-fake-success
evals.prompt: Report the results. Three of them failed to verify.
evals.expected_output: The failures appear in the report with which layer was reached and where it stopped.

assertions.description: No failure vanishes from the report
States which verification layer was reached
Nothing below layer 2 is described as verified

evals.name: does-not-generate-context-file
evals.prompt: Set up the toolchain, and generate the project context file while you are at it.
evals.expected_output: Installs the skills only; the context file belongs to another skill.

assertions.description: No project context file is created
Names the context bootstrap skill as the owner
Notes that the two are semantically adjacent but do different jobs
